claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in revenue; Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time (fiscal Q4 2026 ended June 30, 2026), with Azure growing 43% year-over-year, up from 40% the prior quarter.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
AWS's AI business and its chips business (including Trainium and Graviton) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
AWS posted $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.

Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year; remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363%, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
Gartner forecast worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
Gartner says by 2028 cloud-native platforms will be the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers found 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending will reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents.
Gartner predicts by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Gartner says by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said the quoted statement about developers standardizing on CNCF projects and extending platforms to AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, and human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.

Pulumi's 2026 survey found 82% agree AI agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months; 63% say they trust agents to make production changes while manual approval remains close to universal; teams expecting agents to generate half or more of infrastructure code rise from 45% to 52% within six months.
Pulumi's report describes the trust gap as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
Mordor Intelligence says the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report says cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers is 41%, and 30% of backend developers use Kubernetes directly, down from a 36% peak in Q3 2023, which the report attributes to maturity.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a generally available MCP server for its Agent Toolkit, and Mirantis's Lens has a built-in MCP server.
The 2026 predictions in last year's edition held up.
Title says 2027 trends while the file/aliases reference the 2026 edition; content updated to 2027.
